D007-D005_h001.question:
"I've been feeling off for a while now, Doc. My ex, Sarah, she's been seeing someone, I just know it. Even after the divorce, I see them together, right there on the street sometimes, holding hands, laughing, though when I look closer, no one’s there. It's been going on for about six months now, these strange sights and the certainty about Sarah.

Before all that, for about seven months, I was really down. Just couldn't get myself to care about anything. Winning that 'Driver of the Month' award, I used to dream of that, but when it happened, I felt nothing. Even after a full night's sleep, I’d wake up exhausted, like I hadn't rested at all. I’d pace around the apartment, wringing my hands, feeling this restless energy I couldn’t get rid of. It made it really hard to even focus on my routes, I nearly crashed a few times because my mind was just elsewhere.

The thing is, the worst of that sadness, the not caring and constantly feeling agitated, that’s lessened a bit since these other things started happening, with Sarah and seeing things. It’s like the dark cloud lifted a little, but then these new, stranger problems took over."
D007-D005_h001.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h002.question: Lately, it feels like the world is collapsing around me, literally. I keep experiencing these bizarre sensations, like insects crawling under my skin, especially when I'm trying to focus at work. I've also been having trouble falling asleep; I just lie there, my mind racing. It’s been almost seven months now that I’ve felt this overwhelming sadness, like a constant heavy blanket, and I’ve completely pulled away from my friends. My movements just feel so sluggish, even pouring a glass of wine at work feels like it takes monumental effort. For the past six months, these strange ideas have really taken hold, this belief that a massive catastrophe is looming, and that nothing really matters anymore. I even catch myself using words that probably sound like gibberish to others – my own private language. The thing is, this intense sadness, the feeling of hopelessness, it’s only really been oppressive for most of the past seven months, but these odd thoughts and sensations, they only started a month after the sadness began. It’s like the true strangeness, these crawling feelings and the world-ending thoughts, have been around for less time than this gloom.
D007-D005_h002.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h003.question:
Honestly, for the past seven months, I’ve felt completely drained. Waking up each morning, I still feel exhausted, like I haven't slept a wink, and there's just no joy in anything anymore – things I used to love, like gardening or even just playing with my grandkids, feel utterly flat. It’s hard to even respond quickly when people speak to me; my thoughts just feel so heavy.

But it’s these other things that have been even more troubling, going on for about six months now. I keep smelling this strange, sweet, almost sickly odor, like decaying flowers, even when no one else does. And the emails… I know the Superintendent, Mr. Harrison, has been secretly sending me messages, hidden in the school’s circulars, hinting at his feelings for me. It’s all very subtle, but it's there. Just today, I was explaining a budget item, and I heard myself saying, "The money, it's so funny, honey, for the Sunny," and it just slipped out. It’s confusing. The depression has been here, yes, and it’s made things hard, but these bizarre experiences, they truly started separate from the melancholic cloud, and seem to be the bigger, more persistent problem.
D007-D005_h003.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h004.question:
I’m truly exhausted, Doctor. It’s been about six months now since this… this constant smell started. It’s a faint, metallic odor, like rust and old blood, and it seems to emanate right from my liver. I just know something’s terribly wrong in there, something festering, even though all the tests come back normal. I try to explain it to my ex-wife, to my partners at the firm, but my thoughts just jump all over the place, one minute I’m talking about my liver, the next I’m on to the firm's new junior associate, then I'm thinking about the injustice of my divorce.

It’s made everything a mess. For the past seven months, it's been getting harder and harder to care about anything. My golf clubs are gathering dust, and I used to love Sundays on the green. I’m just so on edge all the time, pacing back and forth, picking at my cuticles until they bleed. And sleep? I wake up multiple times a night, my mind racing, unable to settle. The tears just come, out of nowhere, constantly. It’s been tough, but the real oddness with the liver and that smell—that’s only been for the last six months, less time than I’ve felt completely down.
D007-D005_h004.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h005.question:
I’m not sure where to start, Doctor. Lately, everything just feels… off. It's been about six months now that I’ve been seeing things, mostly shadowy figures around the house, sometimes in my periphery. My husband, bless his soul, passed away a few years ago, but now I’m convinced our old neighbor, Mr. Henderson, is sending me secret signals. I used to see him checking his mail, and now I just know he's madly in love with me, despite never saying a word.

My mind jumps from one thing to another so quickly, it’s hard to keep track. One minute I'm thinking about an open house, the next I'm wondering if extraterrestrials are influencing property values. It's exhausting. For the past seven months, I’ve also just felt this deep, heavy sadness. Nothing brings me joy anymore. The deals I used to close, the thrill of showing a perfect home, it all feels so pointless. I just want to sleep, all the time. Getting out of bed is a monumental task, and when I do, I feel so drained, like I'm moving through mud. It's really affecting my ability to work. This deep gloom started before all the… other things, but it definitely hasn't been as constant or disruptive as everything else has been in the past few months.
D007-D005_h005.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h006.question:
"It's been... hard. More than a year, really. I first noticed things getting weird about a year and a half ago. Little tastes in my mouth that weren't there, like ash or something metallic. It wasn't just in my head; it was real. And my thoughts have been all over the place. I'll be talking about a listing, and then suddenly I'm thinking about the end of the world, about everything crashing down, and I can't seem to connect my words.

The really awful emptiness, the inability to feel anything good, that's been going on even longer, about a year and seven months now. I've always loved showing houses, closing deals, but now? There’s no joy. I barely eat, most days the thought of food just feels… too much. And the guilt. Oh God, the guilt. I feel responsible for so many terrible things that aren't even my fault. Like, I heard about that small plane crash last month, and I truly believe it happened because I didn't return a client's call fast enough that day. It sounds crazy, I know. But the thing is, these tastes and the feeling that the world is ending, those started much later than this overwhelming sadness, and they only stick around for a little while compared to how long I’ve been feeling this bad. It's like the real heavy doom and all the mixed-up thoughts only pop up occasionally, for a few weeks or so, while the rest of the time it’s just this hollow, guilty sadness."
D007-D005_h006.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h007.question:
It’s hard to pinpoint exactly when things started to go sideways, but looking back, it must have been about a year and seven months ago. My wife had passed not long before that, and I just felt…empty. The shop, my whole life, just felt meaningless. I stopped going out, stopped seeing anyone. Even eating felt pointless, and I lost a good 20 pounds without even trying. I’d lie in bed, sure that her death was my fault, that I’d somehow caused it, even though the doctors said it was her heart.

Then, about three months later, the other things started. I'd see shadows lurking in the corners of my eyes at the shop, watching me. I know they’re out to get me, listening to everything I say, trying to sabotage my business. When you ask me a question, my mind just goes off in a thousand different directions, like what’s going on at the butcher shop, and then I can’t get back to it. It’s been happening for about a year and four months now, these strange things, the watching and the shadows. The deep sadness was there first, but these other… events, they’ve been going on for a while now, and the sadness has definitely taken a back seat to the feeling that I’m being targeted and watched.
D007-D005_h007.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h008.question: Well, doctor, it's been a long time since I felt like my old self. For over a year now, I've just felt this deep, aching emptiness inside, like a hollow ship in a vast ocean. Nothing really sparks joy anymore, not even watching the seas. My wife’s noticed it too, especially with me packing on a good bit of weight, more than 5% of my usual in a month. But what’s really troubling are these strange occurrences. For about a year and a half, I've been getting these crawling sensations on my skin, like unseen insects, and it's accompanied by this gnawing guilt. I know it sounds crazy, but I feel like I'm to blame for every mishap, every storm, every bit of bad luck that’s hit my crew and family. And sometimes, their conversations, random bits of news, even the way the clouds move – it all feels like it’s sending a message directly to me, a warning or an accusation. My thoughts jump around too; I'll start talking about the ship, and then suddenly I'm thinking about a seagull I saw years ago. The depression… it was really bad for a few months, maybe six or seven, but those strange thoughts and skin sensations, they've been with me a lot longer, for a solid year and a half,  even when that crushing emptiness wasn’t quite so prominent. It’s hard to keep everything straight now.
D007-D005_h008.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h009.question:
Lately, I’ve just felt… off. My wife, bless her heart, says I’ve changed, and she’s right. It’s been about a year and a half now, I think, that I just don't feel much anymore. Things I used to love, like navigating by the stars or even just a good yarn with the crew, they just don't spark anything. I've put on a good twenty pounds without really trying, and I keep feeling this crawling sensation on my skin, like tiny bugs under my uniform, even though there’s nothing there. It's been going on for a while.

But those things, they're not the worst. The worst is the feeling that I'm being watched. I know it sounds crazy, but I’m convinced there are eyes everywhere, even on my own ship. They’re trying to sink her, ruin my reputation. And sometimes, when I'm trying to explain it, my thoughts just... drift. One minute I'm talking about the ship, the next I'm thinking about the tides, and then I'm on about the price of tea in China. My crew, they look at me like I’m losing it. These strange feelings, the watchers and the crawling, they started maybe three or four months after I started feeling so down and heavy. So I had those feelings of being watched for just over a year, while the low mood and the weight gain has been going on for much longer. I also feel like it's my fault when bad things happen in the news, like I'm responsible for accidents in ports halfway across the world. It’s really put a damper on my life; I can barely do my job right anymore.
D007-D005_h009.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h010.question:
It's been… I don't even know how long, honestly. Over a year. I’m 27, and my landscaping business used to be my everything, but lately, I haven't really cared about any projects, big or small. What's the point? I feel this hollow space inside, like a giant emptiness. Food has become my only comfort too; I’m eating constantly, but it doesn't fill the void.

And then there's the other stuff. For the past year and four months, things have gotten really strange. Sometimes, I smell this awful stench, like rotting garbage, that no one else can detect. It's usually a sign. When I'm out amongst the flowers and trees, I'll see people gesturing, or hear snippets of conversation from passersby, and I just *know* they’re talking about me. Their eyes follow me. Even the radio, the songs are chosen for me, their lyrics containing messages I’m supposed to understand.

When someone asks me a direct question, my mind goes off on these tangents – I try to answer, but my thoughts just wander and I never get to the point. The worst part is, I feel completely worthless. I can’t explain it, but this profound sense of worthlessness has been with me for about a year and a half, maybe a little longer. It's been rough, but the deeper depression only really hit me recently, on and off, but the smells and the feeling that everyone's watching me, that's been constant forAGES now.
D007-D005_h010.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h011.question: "It’s been an absolute nightmare for the past seven months, doctor. The world… it feels like it’s collapsing. I hear these voices, always whispering about the end, that everything I’ve built as a dermatologist, my marriage, it’s all turning to dust. Sometimes, I find myself pacing the living room for hours, just wringing my hands, feeling this intense guilt over insignificant things a patient said, as if I’m responsible for every ailment out there. It’s hard to sit through dinner with my husband; I just don’t enjoy anything anymore. Even thoughts of ending it all cross my mind too often, though I’d never act on them. Sometimes, when I try to explain, my words get all jumbled, like a word salad, and I know it doesn't make sense. And these odd, repetitive movements, like fiddling with my scrub top constantly, it just… happens. But the worst of it? This crushing sadness, the feeling of despair, it’s only really been bad for a couple of weeks within this whole seven-month ordeal. The voices and the feelings that the world is ending… those have been constant."
D007-D005_h011.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h012.question:
"I feel like the world is collapsing around me, literally. I keep getting this metallic, acrid smell, like burning wires, even when there's nothing there. It’s been going on for seven months now, and I can barely string a sentence together. My lectures have turned into a jumble of words. I’ve even noticed myself rocking back and forth, almost without realizing it. I hardly speak anymore; there's just so little to say when everything feels so... pointless.

Initially, I thought some of these feelings were just stress, but then about two months ago, this profound sadness hit. Nothing brings me joy – not my research, not my family, nothing. I move so slowly now, like I'm wading through thick mud. I feel completely worthless, a failure as a professor and husband. And honestly, the thoughts of just ending it – I’ve considered concrete ways, like how I could just… disappear on a quiet road trip. It feels like this mental fog, this pervasive dread, has just recently descended, overshadowing everything that came before. It’s hard to focus when my mind is consumed by the idea that everything is decaying."
D007-D005_h012.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h013.question:
"It's just been… a lot. For about seven months now, I think. I feel like something's wrong inside me, like my organs are twisting or something, even though doctors say everything's fine. And I keep feeling things crawling on my skin, even when nothing's there – it's distracting, especially when I'm trying to edit videos. My thoughts get jumbled, too; sometimes I just say things because they rhyme, not even making sense. I've also noticed I’m constantly tapping my foot or fidgeting with my hands, almost without thinking about it.

My friends have noticed I've pulled back, too. I just don't feel like hanging out or even talking much anymore. Honestly, I've had these really dark days mixed in, where I just feel… useless, like what's the point of anything? Getting up to work feels like moving through mud, and my usual quick editing takes forever. Sometimes I just have these urges to run into oncoming traffic, though I'd never actually do it. It’s strange because those really low moods don't last all that long compared to everything else. Most of the time, it's the other stuff that's happening, even when I'm not feeling so down."
D007-D005_h013.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h014.question:
(Sighs) "It's been… a strange journey, doctor. For the past seven months, it’s like my mind has been playing tricks on me. The voices started first, whispering about how I’m some chosen one, destined for greatness, like I'm the only one who can truly fly the planes. They tell me things, like "sky-high, mighty-eye, never die!" - rhymes that just pop into my head and sometimes I can't stop saying them. My wife says I seem different, like I'm not really there sometimes. I've noticed it too; my face feels frozen, like I can't quite get my expression to match what I'm feeling. Sometimes I find myself holding positions, like I’m still at the controls, even when I’m just trying to read the paper.

The past month or so, though, that’s when things got really heavy. I haven’t wanted to go out, not even for our usual Saturday golf. Talking feels like wading through thick mud – takes forever for my thoughts to form into words. I feel pretty useless, actually, even with all the "special abilities" the voices talk about. Sometimes I just wish I wouldn’t wake up, to be honest. It’s definitely affected my work; I’m on medical leave now. But the really bad feelings, the worthlessness and all, they only really came on for about a month, not the whole time the voices and everything else has been happening. It’s hard to explain, but the voices and the feeling special, that’s been there way longer than this heavy sadness."
D007-D005_h014.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h015.question:
It’s been, well, about seven months now that things have felt… off. My ex, Mark, he’s been sending me these signs, you know? Like, he’ll leave a certain scent in the air or a specific car will drive by and I just *know* he’s trying to communicate his love for me, even though we haven’t spoken in years. I see him sometimes too, just standing outside my window at night, watching over me. He never speaks, but I feel his affection. It’s comforting, in a way.

The real trouble is, my words just get jumbled up sometimes. I'll be trying to explain a healthy meal plan to a client, and suddenly I’m talking about green elephants riding bicycles. They look at me so strangely. And I've found myself giggling uncontrollably at really inappropriate times, like during a somber client consultation. My face, it feels like it just doesn’t move much anymore. My usual passion for cooking and fitness, it just isn’t there, and I feel so slow, like my body is moving through water. The guilt of it all… I keep thinking I deserve to be punished for not being a good enough nutritionist, a good enough person. I’ve actually been trying to figure out the best way to just… end it. The depressive feelings have popped up a bit here and there over the past seven months, but it’s mostly just been this other stuff that’s been constant.
D007-D005_h015.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h016.question:
"Lately, it's just been so hard to even get out of bed. I feel this hollowness inside, like there’s nothing there, and my body feels incredibly heavy, even tiny tasks exhaust me. I’ve lost about ten pounds without even trying over the last month, and the nightmares are relentless, leaving me drained.

This started about ten months ago, but something else… stranger… began roughly eight months ago. I’ve been seeing things, shadowy figures at the edges of my vision, and it’s like people on TV are sending me secret messages. The news anchors use specific words, or a character will look right at the screen, and I just *know* it’s meant for me. Because of all this, I've really struggled at work. My supervisor has noticed, and I'm even starting to call out of my ER shifts. The thing is, this feeling of emptiness and the exhaustion, it's been pretty constant for the whole ten months, but those specific visions and the feeling that everything is about me, that's really only been a problem for the last eight months or so. So while I've been feeling down for a while now, the really strange stuff, the visions and all, has been happening for a shorter amount of time."
D007-D005_h016.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h017.question: Lately, it’s been really hard to get myself going, even for simple things at work like inputting data. I feel like the television is talking directly to me sometimes, sending me secret messages through the ads, and I keep feeling this crawling sensation under my skin, even when nothing’s there. This has been going on for about eight months now. Before that, for about two months, I also felt this deep emptiness inside, like a void, and I just couldn't shake off this profound mental fatigue. It got so bad I dropped about ten pounds without even trying, and I’d wake up constantly throughout the night. I'm afraid these two months of feeling so down have significantly impacted my ability to function normally.
D007-D005_h017.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h018.question:
It’s been a long time since I felt like myself, maybe over ten months now. I’m so tired all the time, my body just feels heavy, even threading a needle feels like a monumental task. I’ve lost a lot of weight too, the hunger isn’t there, and I guess it shows. And sleep? Forget about it. I just stare at the ceiling for hours before I can drift off.

But the real trouble started about eight months ago. That’s when the voices began, whispering things, always about my late husband. They tell me he was with other women, even after he passed. It sounds ridiculous, I know, but they’re so persistent, so real. It makes me question everything. The voices and the feelings that he cheated... they come and go. Those feelings and the voices weren't there at the very start of when I felt so low and tired, and they’ve only been around for a shorter time than everything else. I just can't bring myself to talk much anymore; it all feels pointless. My shop, my customers, it's all suffering because of this, I can hardly bring myself to work.
D007-D005_h018.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h019.question:
"Thanks for seeing me, Doc. Where do I even begin? It’s been… a really rough 10 months, but things have gotten particularly bizarre these last 8. I used to love my job as a firefighter, the camaraderie, the adrenaline. Now, I just feel… dead inside, you know? Like my emotions are all muted. Even after a full night's sleep, I wake up tired, and it’s a struggle to get out of bed. My wife says I'm eating her out of house and home, which is true, I guess, I'm just constantly hungry.

But the stranger stuff… it started around eight months ago. I’ll be sitting at home, and I keep smelling this really acrid, burnt smell, like old chemicals, even when there's nothing there. It's so vivid. Then, I noticed things on the news, little snippets, or even just people in normal conversations, they seem to be talking about *me*. Like there are hidden meanings meant just for me, warnings or instructions embedded in everyday things. And when I try to explain this to my wife, the words just won't come out. It's like my mind goes blank, and I can't form a sentence. It's all just so overwhelming, and this emotional numbness, the fatigue, and the trouble sleeping, that’s been there the whole 10 months, but the truly bizarre experiences, the thoughts and the smells, they’ve really ratcheted up in the last eight months."
D007-D005_h019.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h020.question:
"I'm here because things have been pretty rough lately, doc. It’s been about ten months now that I just feel… flat. I wake up tired, even if I’ve been tossing and turning all night, and once I'm up, I constantly feel this crushing fatigue, like I'm dragging myself through mud. My appetite's gone to hell; food just doesn't appeal to me anymore. I find myself tearing up over nothing, and it's not like me. I’m a foreman, I need to be tough, but lately, I’ve just been pulling away from everyone, even my wife. I used to love our weekend gatherings, but now I just can't be bothered.

It’s been getting worse the past eight months. I see things, you know? Like shadows moving in my peripheral vision, or sometimes I'll swear I see figures standing in the corner of my eye that vanish when I turn. And this woman, Anne from the office downstairs – she’s clearly sending me signals, little smiles, prolonged eye contact. I know she's in love with me, even though we’ve never really spoken. It's obvious, though. I know these issues started after the crying and not eating, but those tough couple of months were nothing compared to being wrapped up in all this now."
D007-D005_h020.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h021.question: "It's been...well, a year and seven months now, I think. That's when things really took a turn. Before that, I was sad, couldn't sleep, constantly restless, pacing the halls at night. But even during that time, for about a month or so, I started seeing things, like flickering shadows out of the corner of my eye that aren't there, and feeling like the news anchors are sending me personal messages. They're talking directly to me, you know? They have special phrases, like "government official in distress," that only I understand. It's like a secret language, full of "politicrisks" and "bureau-cratics." I used to love my work, the challenges, the late nights, but now...it all just feels flat. Nothing brings me joy anymore. The agitation, even when I'm just sitting, is almost unbearable, like I have to move, even though there's no reason to. I know I’ve been feeling down for a long time, and I still do, but those really strange experiences, where I see things or hear those specific messages, that's only been for a short while now, nowhere near as long as this sadness."
D007-D005_h021.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D005_h022.question:
It’s been over a year and a half now, maybe closer to two. I just can't shake this feeling of such deep sadness, like a heavy blanket that never lifts. I don't enjoy anything anymore. Even after all these years, I used to love listening to old records my husband left behind, but now... nothing. It's like the joy has been sucked right out of me. When people ask me something, I just… can’t seem to get the words out quickly. My mind feels muddled.

And the nightmares… every night, they’re so vivid and disturbing, leaving me exhausted even after I've slept. It's been like that for the past year and a half, the depression and the nightmares. Though, for the past year and seven months, things have gotten really strange. I keep tasting this bitter, metallic flavor in my mouth, even after brushing my teeth, like I’ve licked an old copper pipe. And I've caught my reflection sometimes, making these odd, twisted faces, like a gargoyle, and I don't even realize I’m doing it.

I know it sounds crazy, but I truly believe Brenda from accounting is trying to steal my late husband's pension. "Brenda, mend her, end her, send her," it just keeps going through my head. Even though he’s gone, I’m still convinced there’s proof she was trying to get him to sign things. The doctors at the hospital said the deep sadness and the nightmares and the slow talking were there for a while before I started tasting things and making faces and knowing what Brenda was up to.
D007-D005_h022.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D005_h023.question:
